conclusion: Latency-bound. With converters skipped and data always ready (no consumer wait is on the converter or on landing), the per-tile consumer cadence is 1.00 us at 10 warps/scheduler (reproduced on three grids: 680, 256, 136 CTAs) and 0.84 us at 5 warps/scheduler (128 CTAs, residency=1 verified). Halving the warps per scheduler removes 16 % of the tile, not 50 %; every consumer segment shrinks by the same 4-19 % and none halves. The chain is dominated by dependent round trips (mbarrier/xBar handoffs, wgmma drains, shuffle chains), with an issue-arbitration tax of at most ~320 cyc (0.16 us) per tile. Two corrections to the plan: (i) the plan's "136 CTAs = 1 CTA/SM" configuration does NOT give 1 CTA/SM for the traced CTA (136 > 132 SMs; the 4 excess CTAs land on the SMs where CTA 0 runs, smid 124/128, so that run measures 2 CTAs/SM and gives the same 1.00 us as the default) — B=16 n=1 is the valid 1-CTA/SM point; (ii) the plan's absolute thresholds (~1.0 fair-share / ~1.7 latency-bound) assumed a 10-warp baseline of 1.5-1.7 us/tile (62 us / 39 tiles); the measured baseline is 1.00 us, so the ratio, not the absolute value, is the discriminator. Wall = tile-times x 1.0 us + a 6-11 us per-wave fixed cost (fill ~1.1-1.3 us to tile 0, drain, merge) — the multiplier question belongs to P0.3 (57.1 us default = 39 x 1.0 + 18).
